product.family: LED filament candle, E14, clear, high CRI
product.description: the lamps of a reproduction 1880s electrolier (four arms, the porch): 4 LED filament candle lamps, 3000 K, CRI 95, dimmable, one in each cased opal globe on the arms' ring. The fitting's turned patinated-bronze body, arms and globes are the stage's own pieces (Albion's sheet, section 3.8), in Matter's bronze and Lamberts cased opal glass.
product.codeBasis: the maker's product code of the lamp

light.fluxBasis: lamps: 4 bare lamps of 260 lm each; the globes' cased opal, drawn by the stage, passes their light on
light.beamName: filament lamps lighting all round, one at the centre of each globe

electrical.control: phase dimmable: the maker names the Schneider 315 RC regulator and the VaLO wireless series

housing.dimensionBasis: the arms' reach to the globes' centres, 0.505 from the stem, is Albion's drawing of the fitting (sheet section 3.8); the lamp's own size is not published
housing.materials: clear glass bulb over LED filaments, E14 cap, inside a cased opal globe of radius 0.085
housing.mounting: E14 lampholder in each globe's gallery on a scrolled arm

photometricFile.note: A lamp has no luminaire photometry; its light leaves all round it and the cased opal globe is Matter's glass.

sources.title: Ledstore, LED bulb E14 candle, clear, high CRI95, dimmable 4W, 3000K (260 lm, 35 000 h, visible filaments)

unverified: The lamp's dimensions and its distribution are not published; a filament candle lights all round, as the record takes it.
Philips' MASTER glass candles and lusters with CRI 90 (read on Signify's pages) come at 2700 K or dim-to-warm 2200 to 2700 K, not 3000 K, so a smaller maker's lamp stands here.
The fitting itself, a reproduction after the 1880s electroliers, is drawn by the stage; no maker of the whole fitting was chosen.
